concerns: The headline scientific finding rate is established by the same LLM-based knowledge audit that the framework optimizes toward, and the manuscript reports no independent validation of that audit's classifications.

The manuscript does not establish that the LLM reviewers used for hypothesis quality are independent of the generation and selection signals, and the reported preference analysis shows evaluator self-preference tendencies.
The external cohort replications corroborate only three selected case studies, not the headline 95.24% scientific finding rate or the claimed superiority over baselines.
scholarly_quality.concise_summary: DeepQuest provides a comprehensive, technically sound, and empirically verified agent workflow for biomedical discovery. The combination of multi-model LLM evaluation, ablation studies, and external clinical validation on ADNI and AIBL provides substantial scientific rigor.

Automating experiments does not necessarily advance scientific understanding.
Research agents must identify meaningful knowledge gaps, determine what avail-
able data can resolve, and assess whether their findings advance existing knowl-
edge. We introduce DeepQuest, a knowledge-gap-driven AI scientist framework
for Alzheimer's disease research. DeepQuest transforms unresolved questions
from domain reviews into traceable, testable hypotheses and prioritizes them
through data feasibility screening and groupwise Elo ranking. It couples itera-
tive experimentation with two-level auditing that separates experimental reliability
from knowledge contribution relative to two frozen literature corpora. On OASIS-
3, DeepQuest produces 42 feasible hypotheses and outperforms the strongest base-
lines in 14 of 15 evaluator–dimension comparisons across three language-model
reviewers. The full

evidence.excerpt:
framework achieves an audit-assessed scientific finding rate
of 95.24%, outperforming both general-purpose executors and domain-specific
research agents. This scientific finding rate remains stable across literature cor-
pora and evaluator model families. Representative findings concern neuropsy-
chiatric symptoms and dementia risk, longitudinal amyloid spatial stability, and
neocortical tau-associated clinical impairment, with key associations supported in
independent ADNI and AIBL cohorts. These results show how aligning knowl-
edge gaps, data feasibility, and evidence auditing can turn automated research into
traceable, evidence-supported scientific discovery. Our source code is available at
https://anonymous.4open.science/r/DeepQuest-3066/.

evidence.excerpt:
The literature evidence repository provides a traceable reference for comparing experimental conclu-
sions against prior research.We decompose clinical studies on AD and related topics into individual
finding entries to construct the evidence repositoryKwhere each entrye∈Krecords the core
claim, boundary and excerpt. This repository defines the literature scope against which subsequent
knowledge contribution is assessed.
Evidence sufficiency is assessed before literature comparison to distinguish interpretable conclu-
sions from insufficiently supported results. Results are labeled as Uncertain when valid evidence
is lacking because of inadequate statistical power, unstable estimates, nonestimable parameters, or
incomplete analysis. Conclusions supported by evidence, including directional associations, condi-
tional differences, or null effects, proceed to literature comparison.

on relation structure, claim direction, and scope. Claims consistent with existing evidence and
introducing no new proposition are labeled Rediscovery. Those revealing additional temporal, inter-
action, nonlinear, spatial, or population-specific patterns are labeled Extension. Claims are labeled
Candidate New Discovery when the retrieved evidence contains no direct precedent for the same un-
derlying relationship or only broadly related precedents. DeepQuest retains the supporting rationale
and source literature. Candidate New Discovery denotes potential knowledge gain relative to the
retrieved evidence from the frozen repository, without establishing the absence of precedents in the
broader literature. Execution auditing assesses procedural consistency, whereas

DeepQuest achieves the highest overall mean across all three evaluators, with its strongest gains
concentrated in dimensions related to scientific question formulation and empirical discriminative
power. Overall improvements over each evaluator's best baseline are 0.27, 0.24, and 0.21 points,
as shown in Fig. 3. DeepQuest outperforms the best baseline in 14 of 15 evaluator–dimension
comparisons. The largest gains are 0.35 in empirical discriminative power under GPT-5.6-sol, 0.34
in novelty under Claude Opus 4.8, and 0.26 in scientific advancement under DeepSeek-v4-pro-
0813. Clinical significance shows relatively smaller gains than other evaluated dimensions: under
GPT-5.6-sol, DeepQuest scores 3.43 versus the best baseline's 3.45.

evidence.excerpt:
The full DeepQuest pipeline achieves the highest SFR across the evaluated general-purpose and
domain-specific agents. Of 42 tasks, 40 yield Candidate New Discovery or Extension, giving an SFR
of 95.24%, compared with 78.57% for Codex and 76.19% for Claude Code on the same DeepQuest-
H hypothesis set, as shown in Table 1. Among the domain-specific baselines, DiscoADRD and
Biomni achieve SFRs of 45.45% and 86.49%, respectively, on their evaluated task sets. These gains
reflect the complete system and cannot be attributed to a single module.
Table 1: Discovery outcome comparison across methods. Candidate New denotes Candidate New
Discovery. Scientific Finding Rate (SFR) represents the proportion of tasks classified as Candidate
New Discovery, Rediscovery, or Extension. Top-10 SFR is computed among the highest-ranked
DeepQuest-H tasks. N/A indicates not applicable.

tween higher neocortical tau and faster clinical progression. MMSE slope associations coefficients
were -0.2113 (-0.3890, -0.0335) in OASIS-3 and -0.0583 (-0.1470, 0.0304) in ADNI, indicating
longitudinal association replication

blocking_reasons: The headline scientific finding rate is established by the same LLM-based knowledge audit that the framework optimizes toward, and the manuscript reports no independent validation of that audit's classifications.

The manuscript does not establish that the LLM reviewers used for hypothesis quality are independent of the generation and selection signals, and the reported preference analysis shows evaluator self-preference tendencies.
The external cohort replications corroborate only three selected case studies, not the headline 95.24% scientific finding rate or the claimed superiority over baselines.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: External ADNI and AIBL cohort replications support three selected case-study associations, but no independent measurement validates the audit-assessed scientific finding rate or the knowledge contribution labels.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: The headline outcome is the audit-assessed scientific finding rate and knowledge contribution labels produced by LLM evaluators against frozen literature corpora.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The framework is shaped by LLM-based data feasibility screening, Elo ranking, execution auditing, and literature-based knowledge contribution auditing.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims regarding superior scientific finding rates, hypothesis quality, and discovery feasibility are well supported by tabulated experimental runs, ablations, and rigorous external cohort replications for the case studies.
primary.evaluation_assessment: Evaluation covers multiple dimensions: hypothesis scoring by multiple distinct LLM families against five baselines, comparative execution outcomes against general and domain-specific agents, ablation of system components, and independent replication of three substantive clinical findings on external ADNI and AIBL cohorts.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Headline claims of valid scientific discoveries and associations are corroborated by external cohort replications (ADNI and AIBL) with standard epidemiological and imaging models (Cox, AFT, LME, clr multivariate regressions), as well as reproduction of published findings.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Evaluation relies on independent LLM evaluators (e.g., Claude Opus 4.8, DeepSeek-v4-pro, GPT-5.6 variants) assessing quality dimensions, audit classification against two frozen literature corpora, and external statistical replication on OASIS-3, ADNI, and AIBL data.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Hypotheses and analytical plans are screened and ranked using automated data feasibility gating, within-system Elo comparative scoring, and iterative execution auditing.

primary.limitations: The authors transparently report that clinical significance scores show smaller gains over baselines, that Top-10 ranking metrics are descriptive due to subset nesting, and that candidate discoveries remain bounded by the retrieved coverage of the reference literature corpora.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is clearly defined, detailing structured limitation extraction from domain reviews, cohort data feasibility gating, Elo-based comparative prioritization, sandboxed execution with auditing, and dual-query literature comparison (using SPECTER2 embeddings and retrieval against frozen clinical study corpora).
primary.quality_rationale: DeepQuest provides a comprehensive, technically sound, and empirically verified agent workflow for biomedical discovery. The combination of multi-model LLM evaluation, ablation studies, and external clinical validation on ADNI and AIBL provides substantial scientific rigor.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper presents DeepQuest, an agentic framework for Alzheimer's disease research that translates review-extracted knowledge gaps into feasible hypotheses, prioritizes them via Elo ranking, executes multi-round cohort data analyses, and audits knowledge contributions relative to frozen literature reference sets.

scholarly_quality.rationale: DeepQuest provides a comprehensive, technically sound, and empirically verified agent workflow for biomedical discovery. The combination of multi-model LLM evaluation, ablation studies, and external clinical validation on ADNI and AIBL provides substantial scientific rigor.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors transparently report that clinical significance scores show smaller gains over baselines, that Top-10 ranking metrics are descriptive due to subset nesting, and that candidate discoveries remain bounded by the retrieved coverage of the reference literature corpora.
